_about: Public-domain Moses Stuart (1780-1852, professor of sacred literature at Andover Theological Seminary) for the Word Hoard: his commentaries on Romans (1832), Hebrews (1833), the Apocalypse (1845, 2 vols), Daniel (1850), Ecclesiastes (1851) and Proverbs (1852) and A Letter to William E. Channing on Religious Liberty (1830), raw Internet Archive OCR. Added 2026-10-03 by lane A, round 10 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. No uids minted.

mstuart-romans-1832: A Commentary on the Epistle to the Romans (Andover: Flagg and Gould, 1832)
mstuart-hebrews-1833: A Commentary on the Epistle to the Hebrews (Andover: Flagg, Gould and Newman, 1833)
mstuart-apocalypse-1845-v1: A Commentary on the Apocalypse, vol. 1 (Andover: Allen, Morrill and Wardwell, 1845)
mstuart-apocalypse-1845-v2: A Commentary on the Apocalypse, vol. 2 (Andover: Allen, Morrill and Wardwell, 1845)
mstuart-daniel-1850: A Commentary on the Book of Daniel (Boston: Crocker and Brewster, 1850)
mstuart-ecclesiastes-1851: A Commentary on Ecclesiastes (New York: G. P. Putnam, 1851)
mstuart-proverbs-1852: A Commentary on the Book of Proverbs (New York: M. W. Dodd, 1852)
mstuart-letter-channing-1830: A Letter to William E. Channing, D.D., on the Subject of Religious Liberty (Boston: Perkins and Marvin, 1830)

_alternates.mstuart-hebrews-1827: the first edition of the Hebrews commentary (1827-28, 2 vols), IA acommentaryonep03unkngoog / acommentaryonep02stuagoog

_excluded.mstuart-hebrew-grammars: the Hebrew Grammar (1821-31) and Hebrew Chrestomathy (1829-38): grammars of Hebrew whose OCR text layers drop the Hebrew, so the text is not usable
_excluded.mstuart-nt-grammar-1841: A Grammar of the New Testament Dialect (1841), IA agrammarnewtest01stuagoog: fetched and measured 2026-10-03, its text layer has 0 Greek characters (84.5% OCR), so a Greek grammar without its Greek; not shelved
